subject: Confirmation: account erase criteria, backup constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmation: account erase criteria, backup constraints & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with FinBank's requirements around erase/RTBF requests.

Call highlights (summary):
- Scope: erase for user accounts under the corporate umbrella (customer_id: FTB-9821).
- PII categories called out: names, emails, account metadata, and user-generated content sent to Redwood models.
- Compliance ask: ability to provide an auditable attest that data was removed and instructions on how backups are handled.

Questions we need from you to finalize the plan:
1) Which PII categories must be included in a standard RTBF (we captured the four above; please add if we missed any).
2) Required retention windows (e.g., 30 days for logs, 90 days for audit records) and any statutory minimums we must observe.
3) Whether an attestation via deletion-job run IDs + S3 manifest is acceptable, or if you require signed/legal confirmation.
4) Any regulatory constraints for cross-border deletion (we noted FinBank uses cloud regions in us-east and eu-west).

Notes on backups and practical constraints (so expectations are clear):
- Production objects: we can remove primary copies immediately per the deletion job.
- Snapshot/backups: standard snapshot lifecycle can leave immutable deltas for between 7–30 days depending on account policy and vendor snapshot dedupe logic; we usually see 7–30 days before immutable recovery windows expire.
- For stricter timelines we can offer an accelerated purge path (isolated-offline purge + attest) but this requires a signed agreement and an ops maintenance window and may incur additional engineering hours.

Proposed timeline (subject to your answers above):
- Acknowledgement of RTBF request & scope confirmation: 48 hours.
- Primary data deletion and audit evidence creation: 72 hours from acknowledged request.
- Backup/snapshot purge window: standard 7–30 days; optional accelerated path target: 7 business days with agreed scope & exec approval.

Attachments: redwood-erase-process-overview.pdf (process flow), retention-matrix.csv (examples of retention windows by artifact).

Next steps / asks:
- Sara: confirm PII categories and whether the accelerated 7-day target is required, or if the standard snapshot window is acceptable.
- If acceptable, can FinBank legal (legal@finbank.com) confirm the list of evidence items needed for your audit trail?
- I'll create a short MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones and attach for signature.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15m call with Security/Legal if that helps.

Best,

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PII: please add device identifiers and IP addresses to the PII list.
2) Retention windows: legal requires logs kept for 90 days (for fraud investigations) but prefers primary data purged within 30 days of request where possible.
3) Evidence: FinBank Legal prefers a combination of (a) deletion job IDs and timestamped manifests, and (b) an attestation letter signed by the vendor for each purge.
4) Backups: our security team is pushing for a 3–7 day maximum snapshot retention for customer-initiated erasures. Is 3 days realistic?

We attached a short list of required fields for the attestation to this thread (see attachment: SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf).

Can we aim for the accelerated path (7 business days)? 3 days would be ideal but I know that’s tight — if you can confirm feasibility and any cost/ops implications we can table it for legal review.

— Sara

Sara / Camila — looping in a few legal/ops clarifications from our side (high level):

- Backups: standard infrastructure snapshots have a technical imprint (deduped blocks and incremental deltas). For most clients we can guarantee primary object deletion immediately and provide manifests. Immutable snapshots from the cloud vendor can persist up to 30 days depending on provider and region.
- Accelerated purge: we can offer an accelerated purge (target 7 business days) that includes: isolated purge job, removal of searchable KV caches, and a signed attestation. This will require a scoped work order and a one-time ops fee. 3-day full snapshot purge is generally infeasible with our current provider contracts unless the provider supports immediate snapshot tombstoning — we can investigate but it’s not a standard offering.
- Evidence: acceptable items are: deletion-job id + UTC timestamp, S3 bucket manifest showing object keys removed, and a signed attestation PDF from Redwood (we'll provide the template).
- Exceptions: any request that requires purging backups earlier than 7 days will need legal sign-off and potentially vendor coordination (may push timeline to 10–14 days).

Camila — I recommend we send the MAP with two tracks: "standard" (primary deletion + 30-day snapshot exposure) and "accelerated" (7 business days + attestation + fees). Sara — if you can confirm which track FinBank prefers we’ll prep the formal paperwork.

Lauren Bishop
